The opened whole-word entries do not explicitly state that its modern meaning is composed from separate contributions by 乱 and 暴.

A cautious modern component gloss is that 乱 is compatible with a disorderly or unruly quality, while 暴 is compatible with rough, forceful, or violent behavior. The opened sources differ in certainty about 暴’s graphic history: 字通 presents an account involving exposed animal remains, whereas the Taishukan reference says the formation is unclear and presents that account as one among multiple theories. claims.text_en: 誰（だれ） is an indefinite person pronoun referring to someone whose name or identity is unknown or unclear. The dictionary also records its use in 誰か for an unspecified person and in 誰も with negation for a comprehensive negative meaning.

It describes だれ as becoming general in the early-modern period and says the shift is thought to date from its later part; a historical-language paper likewise contrasts older タレ with ダレ and treats ダレ as unavailable in ancient-to-medieval materials. These sources support a change in reading, but do not prove a deeper derivation or component analysis of the Japanese pronoun.

claims.text_en: For present-day use, explain 一生懸命 as acting with great effort and earnest commitment; depending on context, it can also carry a desperate or life-risking sense. The dictionaries support these meanings, including examples of working and searching 一生懸命. Treat it as an established whole-word meaning.

The older form 一所懸命 referred to a medieval holding or estate that was a basis of livelihood and was defended at risk of life. It later had a figurative sense of urgent, desperate, or life-risking action. The dictionary’s cited examples date the landholding sense to 1212–15 and the figurative sense to 1660; these are cited attestations, not proof of the expression’s first use.

Dictionaries identify 一生懸命 as a changed form of 一所懸命 and cite an example of the modern form from 1734. Their proposed account connects the form change with the fading of the place/estate association and the generalized desperate-effort sense. The precise steps and causes are proposed word-history explanations, not established by the citation dates alone.

Do not teach 一生 as reliably contributing the compositional meaning ‘one’s whole life’ in present-day 一生懸命. The sources define the compound as a whole. One dictionary proposes that changed associations of 一生, including its use for something momentous or occurring once in a lifetime, may have helped motivate the form; other explanations emphasize sound similarity and familiarity. These accounts do not establish ‘one’s whole life’ as the modern compound’s literal meaning.

A narrowly supported component note can say that 一所 in the older form referred to one place or holding, and that the familiar 一生懸命 developed from that older expression as its place-related sense weakened. Do not split the modern compound into independent literal contributions to gloss its current meaning.

investigation_questions.question: Does 緒 contribute a reliable modern meaning to 一緒, or is its character-level association with connection non-compositional here?

guides.explanation_en: 一緒 means doing something together or being in someone’s company. Dictionaries connect it with 一所, meaning one place or the same place, which offers a useful bridge to the shared sense; they do not establish that 一 contributes this meaning compositionally in the modern word. 緒 is associated at the character level with connection or continuation, but its contribution to 一緒’s modern meaning is not established.

parts.contribution_en: The word’s dictionary-attested connection with 一所 (one place; the same place) helps bridge to its shared sense, but a separate modern contribution from 一 is not established.
Character references associate 緒 with connection or continuation, but do not establish that it contributes this meaning to 一緒.

sources.title: 一緒（読み）イッショ — コトバンク／デジタル大辞泉
sources.summary_en: Defines 一緒 as combining things into one, being identical, doing the same thing together, accompanying someone, or happening at the same time. The entry explicitly says it is from 一所. It does not explain the contribution of 緒.

sources.title: 一所（読み）イッショ — コトバンク／精選版 日本国語大辞典
sources.summary_en: Records 一所 as ‘one place’ and ‘the same place.’ For the set of forms 一所・一緒, it gives senses including becoming one, acting alike or together, and grouping things. It labels 一所 as the current form in that section and cites examples from 1688 and 1719.

sources.title: 緒 — 漢字一字 | 漢字ペディア
sources.summary_en: Lists 緒 senses including beginning, line/continuation/connection, heart, and cord; 一緒 appears among its examples for the line/continuation/connection sense. This is a character-level gloss and does not establish that this sense composes the modern word’s meaning or its historical origin.

sources.title: 緒（読み）ショ — コトバンク／デジタル大辞泉・精選版 日本国語大辞典・普及版 字通
sources.summary_en: The Japanese dictionary entries give 緒 senses including thread or cord, a thread’s end, beginning or clue, and continuation. The separate 字通 character analysis discusses the character’s form and senses. Neither entry explains 一緒 as people or things joined on one cord.

claims.text_en: For the supplied sense, 一緒 is lexicographically defined as doing the same thing together; the dictionary also records accompaniment as a related use. This supports the gloss ‘together; in company with someone.’

The dictionaries describe 一緒 as deriving from 一所, and the historical dictionary records 一所・一緒 for senses that include acting together and grouping into one. It also records earlier meanings of 一所 as one place or the same place. This supports reporting a dictionary-attested connection with 一所; it does not by itself establish every step in the word’s historical development.

A character reference associates 緒 with a line, continuation, or connection sense and lists 一緒 as an example. That association may be reported as a character-level gloss, but the opened references do not establish that 緒 contributes ‘connection’ compositionally to the modern word. They do not support explaining 一緒 literally as people or things joined on one cord.

台所 is the ordinary word for a kitchen, the space where food is prepared and cooked. It is conventionally linked to the older name 台盤所 for a room associated with a 台盤, a food-serving stand; this historical shortening is proposed rather than established.

claims.text_en: The consulted dictionaries and JAANUS give 台盤所 as the conventional proposed source of 台所, but phrase the historical connection as an abbreviation or a believed/thought origin. The dictionary dates the shortening to medieval times or later; the materials consulted do not establish a proven derivation.

At the level of 台盤所, 台盤 denotes a legged food-serving stand or low table, and 所 denotes the place where it is set. This supports a compound-level explanation of 台盤所; it does not establish 台 alone as meaning ‘kitchen’ or as independently naming a kitchen space.

The entries distinguish early contexts: 台盤所 is cited from 宇津保物語 (c. 970–999) and described as a palace room for female attendants and food service; 台所 is cited for a cooking and food-service room in 吾妻鏡 (1203). These attestations show the terms in different contexts but do not by themselves demonstrate that one developed from the other.

guides.explanation_en: 交番 also means “taking turns.” Its police-box sense is shortened from 交番所 and is commonly explained as referring to officers taking turns on watch, though that naming link is conjectural.

These dictionary entries give definitions and cited attestations, not direct evidence for why 交番所 was named.

The account supports the associated work practice but does not state that this is why the location was named.

sources.title: 交番まめ知識 | 警視庁

As a standalone conjunction, ところが introduces something contrary to what the preceding situation led you to expect. A modern functional analysis treats ところ as evoking that situation and contrastive が as marking the unexpected turn. This use differs from clause-linking ところが, which has a different grammatical structure.

Marks contrast with those circumstances.

claims.text_en: As a standalone conjunction, ところが introduces content contrary to what the preceding statement leads one to expect. This matches the supplied translation “however; but”; the particular expectation in the supplied sentence depends on its preceding context.

A modern functional analysis treats the conjunction as ところ plus contrastive が: ところ evokes the situation or preceding circumstance, while が marks contrast, yielding a link to an unexpected development. This is an analysis of present function, not proof of the word’s historical derivation.

The conjunction should be distinguished from clause-linking ところが. The dictionary analyzes the latter as formal noun ところ plus case particle が after past た, with uses including a discovery or result and a counterfactual concession; it notes that modern Japanese usually uses ところで for the concessive use.
